dedupe_keys.name: slate ptp datacentre spine leaf timestamp and evaluation benchmark

description: SLATE-PTP records IEEE 1588 timestamps in a physical datacentre testbed with two spine and four leaf switches. University of Granada researchers discipline the capture clock with a GNSS-derived reference while leaving the PTP daemon free-running, to separate network delay effects from local oscillator drift. Four packet-size distributions and constant, stepped or ramped loads produce CSV telemetry. Zenodo distributes the data with a Jupyter evaluation pipeline in a ZIP archive. Data are free under CC BY 4.0; the article states MIT for the included evaluation code. Coverage is one non-PTP-aware switching fabric, with experiments from thirty to nine hundred minutes and exact calendar dates unestablished. Chosen hardware and traffic profiles are limitations for other datacentres. A reviewer-assessed use is testing delay filters and clock-estimation components in network simulations. platform-ns-3 is a related simulator. No telemetry archive, notebook or timing hardware was executed.
